_comment: The entry to add under "funcs" in sql/dialects/<dialect>.json. Shown here
as a standalone file so the documentation can quote it; in the tree it is a
key inside the dialect's existing funcs object.
There is no ANSI spelling for an English ordinal suffix, so this is declared
per dialect rather than on a base -- which is exactly the case sql/MAP.md
describes for LEFT: 'no ANSI spelling; each server has its own'.
ret is required: the translator infers kinds and will not guess. No caveat,
because CONCAT of a CASE over MOD is exact on both servers -- but that is a
claim the oracle has to settle, not a comment.

ORD_SUFFIX.tpl: CONCAT({0}, CASE WHEN MOD({0}, 100) BETWEEN 11 AND 13 THEN 'th' WHEN MOD({0}, 10) = 1 THEN 'st' WHEN MOD({0}, 10) = 2 THEN 'nd' WHEN MOD({0}, 10) = 3 THEN 'rd' ELSE 'th' END)
(CAST({0} AS TEXT) || CASE WHEN MOD({0}, 100) BETWEEN 11 AND 13 THEN 'th' WHEN MOD({0}, 10) = 1 THEN 'st' WHEN MOD({0}, 10) = 2 THEN 'nd' WHEN MOD({0}, 10) = 3 THEN 'rd' ELSE 'th' END)
